question: does screenshot injection hold at full web-small scale (240 questions, all strata)?
design: full-population paired A/B (no sampling): all 87 vision-needed + all 153 text-recoverable web questions, both arms on glm-5.3-flash with glm-5.3 judge, up to 6 anchored screenshots per question, plain hybrid retrieval shared between arms. Same protocol as the 80-question slice.
findings: The text arm reproduces the archived firstpoint baseline exactly (0.1583), validating the pipeline.
Screenshot injection lifts the full web-small tier by +19.2pp overall; BOTH strata gain - text-recoverable +22.2pp and vision-needed +13.8pp.

CORRECTION to the 80-question slice: its vision-needed stratum showed -2.5pp, but the full 87-question population shows +13.8pp - the slice's n=40 VN signal was sampling variance (same lesson as the v13.1 ku-pool mid-run projection). Full-population numbers supersede the slice's stratum-level conclusion.
Vision-needed here is an upper-bound proxy (answer absent from haystack TEXT); a share of those answers still live on retrievable pages, which is exactly where screenshots help.
honest_reading: recall-marker-free full protocol with answerer+judge; the retrieval bottleneck conclusion narrows to the residual: questions whose answer page is never ranked into top-12 still cannot benefit. plain (non-orchestrated) retrieval, shared by both arms, so the A/B delta is attributable to the screenshots alone.
